correctness.rationale: Explicit trigonometric moment-equation inversion yields W=(2 pi/S)(sin b,sin c,sin a) with strictly positive S. A gap exceeds pi if and only if its associated weight is negative; the three bad events are mutually exclusive and each independent-uniform difference has an exact triangular tail. At alpha=1/2 only pair-collision square corners are singular, with weights of order one over the sum of their two nonnegative corner distances. Their p-moment is finite exactly for p<2. Uniform local expansions, the integrable 1/(Delta+u+v) remainder and exact tangent-square integral prove the displayed coefficient and O(1) remainder. The standalone verifier passed 251 reproducible numeric and symbolic checks, not used in place of the analytic proof.

value.rationale: This is the smallest natural nontrivial periodic interpolatory quadrature, directly motivated by published large-grid questions about negative weights and conditioning. The result completely characterizes the positivity event and all weight moments under a natural independent perturbation model; its distinct 1/4 positivity and 1/2 noise-variance transitions inform a precise perturbation-versus-stability design decision. The logarithmic constant controls sample-noise amplification as nodes approach collision and is not supplied by generic upper bounds. No broader theorem or unproved application is asserted.
